schema: functions: name -> file, orig, size_orig, status (open, exact), kind, callers, note (by hand: an odd source form, a guessed name, dead code).

main.note: WEGA 1.5 (02/28/84), not the local.c 1.3 of ZEUS: no getlogin test; the X request (a command for the local system: the arguments joined by argcat, sent with a check byte until ACK, 10 tries; ENQ brings two bytes of an exit status, else 0x8000 and CAN). The names of the globals are those of the symbol table of the original (targ, targsave, i, rc, acknak, checksum, commnd: rc stands in front of acknak in the symbol table, so it is declared there); argc <= 1 for the quit request (jr gt), the retry loop tests NAK on top and the count at the bottom.

argcat.note: name from the symbol table; s and t are never used: the original has two unused frame words (at 4 and 8: s, p, t in one declaration); buf and nargv are static (no symbol); + in front of the first argument or of argv[0] and % in front of a later one decide whether the letters go to upper case (toupper of libc)

note: Exact. A Zilog binary as it seems: the SCCS line has its path and its trailer overwritten (aaaaaaaaaaaabbbb/local.c, ............), as the WEGA developers patched the Zilog marks out of the ZEUS binaries (owner); the line is kept in the source as the bytes have it. Built in one step by cc (/lib/crt0.o, a symbol table, cc.3998.o: patched in by the Makefile as for putud) with the compiler and libc of Zilog of 1984: the cparse of ZEUS 3.21 (/lib/cparse) puts the static buf and nargv of argcat into the .bss (ccvz, OLD_D12B: the same object), and the libc has _NFILE 40 and the data, filbuf, doscan, printf, doprnt, malloc of the libc.a of ZEUS 3.21 (libc-v14, every member from C, byte-identical with the ZEUS members). The whole ZEUS chain (/bin/cc of zeus321_root) gives the same binary. The corpus runs the protocol on the standard input.
